B0.label: Files
B0.represents: How Claude Code (CLAUDE.md, auto-memory, agent-team task list) and Hermes (MEMORY.md, kanban, files) coordinate today
B0.description: MEMORY.md + JSON task list under inter-process file locks (flock), atomic os.replace writes, append-only per-agent JSONL logs
B0.isolation: one directory per tenant; the tenant name is validated before it becomes a path

B1.label: SQLite
B1.description: SQLite in WAL mode, BEGIN IMMEDIATE transactions, FTS5 recall, recursive CTEs for provenance
B1.isolation: one SQLite database file per tenant; the tenant name is validated before it becomes a path

B2.label: Vector
B2.description: Same local bge-small embeddings as Plexus, stored in SQLite + numpy brute-force cosine. Hybrid: claims, decisions and handoffs use B1's SQLite tables because a vector store cannot do atomic claims
B2.isolation: one SQLite database file (facts + vectors) per tenant; the tenant name is validated before it becomes a path

P.label: Plexus
P.represents: Plexus: FalkorDB 6.0.2, one graph per tenant, deterministic Cypher
P.description: Engram/Relay/Lineage service layer called directly (memory, decision and handoff calls also write Steps and READ/WROTE edges)
P.isolation: one FalkorDB graph per tenant (plexus_t_<tenant>); the tenant is bound at construction, never taken from a tool argument, and validated against ^[a-z0-9_]{1,48}$

honesty: L2: exact-match accuracy over a script-derived question set (43 questions, 10 families), one scenario, one model, one run per question; no LLM judge anywhere. Ground truth is computed from the scenario script, not read back from any arm.

Baselines are the same unmodified `claude -p` with no tools, shown their own artifacts at the same 32,000-character cap. At this scenario size the B0 and B1 artifacts fit in the cap without truncation, so the cap is not what limits them; B2 deliberately sees only its top-12 retrieved chunks.

Arm P answers each question with a hand-written Cypher statement per question family. That is the point of the comparison (a graph can answer these with one query) but it is also engineering effort the baselines do not get: the baselines were given no hand-written SQL or grep helpers either.

The Procedures family of BASELINE §2 is not in this set: the backend protocol has no procedure tool, so the arms cannot be compared on it. Cross-session recall is reduced to episodes recorded by agents (the protocol has no sessions).

The scenario is the P3 Acme script replayed on the backend protocol, plus three L2 additions (the forum-post poison fault, one extra builder decision, two project-scoped facts); see crucible/l2/scenario.py.

B1 and B2 (and B0's task file) keep only a task's final claimer, not the claim history; only B0's per-agent logs and Plexus's CLAIMED edges record who held an expired lease. Recovery questions therefore test what each arm's artifacts actually contain, as configured in L1.
